comments.note: FilterSlot.SlotId uses 'required init'. The 'new insert vs update' distinction in SaveAsync relies on SlotId being zero or unrecognised — this contract is documented in XML comments but is implicit and unenforceable at the type level. Downstream implementations must document or enforce this convention.
IActiveFilterSlotRepository exposes only a getter. A caller cannot clear or set the active slot through this interface; future work will need a setter (noted by Developer as known design gap).

comments.note: All three Core files are minimal, focused, and consistent with existing project patterns (sealed record with required init properties, interface-first with CancellationToken defaults). No issues found.

IFilterSlotRepository XML comment correctly documents the insert/update convention. The 'or unrecognised' qualifier is appropriate at the interface level — it gives the implementation latitude to handle non-zero SlotIds that don't exist in the DB. This is a deliberate design choice, not ambiguity.

The 'new insert' convention (SlotId == 0) is implicit and not type-enforced. Both Developer and QA have flagged this. A future refactor could introduce a CreateFilterSlot / UpdateFilterSlot discriminated union or factory method pattern to make the intent explicit at the call site — but this is a future improvement, not a current defect.
